'''Ikanashi Shrine''' (伊加奈志神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Imabari|Imabari]], {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|qid=Q123376|lt=Ehime Prefecture|1=Ehime Prefecture}}, Japan. It is considered a provincial shrine (総社) of {{ill|Iyo Province|en|Iyo Province|qid=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province|1=Iyo Province}} and a {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} shrine.
== Enshrined Deities ==
* Five Pillars of Creation (Five Heavenly Kami)
* Ikatarashihiko-no-Mikoto (いかたらしひこのみこと), identified as a prince of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}
* Ikagasikooro-no-Mikoto (いかがしこおのみこと), believed to be an ancestral deity of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan|qid=Q1755836|lt=Mononobe clan|1=Mononobe clan}}
== History ==
The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} under {{ill|Ochi District, Ehime|en|Ochi District, Ehime|qid=Q1206502|lt=Ochi District, Iyo Province|1=Ochi District, Ehime}}. Historically known as "Sosha Myojin" (総社明神), the shrine's proximity to the Soja River (蒼社川) reflects its importance as a regional spiritual center. The name "Ikanashi" is thought to derive from "Ikagasiko," a reference to the enshrined deity.
The shrine's documents and treasures were lost in a fire during the {{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|qid=Q1327259|lt=Ansei era|1=Ansei}} (1854–1860).

The nearby summit of the mountain hosts {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine (Imabari)|ja|石清水八幡神社 (今治市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine (Imabari)|1=Iwashimizu-Hachiman Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55535314}}.
== festivals ==
The shrine's festival takes place on October 10. A lottery system determines the heads of the shrine's organizing groups (10-household units) for the following year, and the festival is led by the selected leader (当屋). A kagami (mirror) ritual and mochi offering are central components.
In addition to the festival, an early seedling festival (早苗祭) is held around {{ill|88th night|ja|八十八夜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/88th night|1=Hachijūhachiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11390609}}, when prayers for a bountiful harvest are made.
